focus: Traceability — requirements, acceptance evidence, and report consumers

findingDetails.title: Progressive JSON mode merges the skip notice into stdout
findingDetails.evidence: When JSON mode is on, the wrapper captures validate.sh with 2>&1 and prints that capture unchanged when pipeline level 1 is final. validate.sh writes its skip notice to stderr and its JSON report to stdout, so the wrapper's stdout begins with prose and is not parseable JSON. At higher levels the generated JSON uses only the zero exit code and omits a skipped field. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/progressive-validate.sh:262-274] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/progressive-validate.sh:610-672] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/validate.sh:142-172]
findingDetails.recommendation: Keep stderr separate from the JSON payload and propagate an explicit skipped status in every progressive JSON response; add wrapper-level coverage for level 1 and the aggregate levels.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The packet's affected-surface table names progressive-validate.sh and says it passes validate.sh output through; the wrapper's JSON branch instead merges stderr with stdout. REQ-005 promises parseable JSON for a skipped JSON run.

claimAdjudication.claim: Progressive JSON output is malformed for a skipped run at pipeline level 1 because the stderr notice is merged into the JSON stdout payload.
claimAdjudication.counterevidenceSought: The plan labels progressive-validate.sh unchanged and describes output as passthrough; inspected the actual JSON capture and producer channel behavior. No channel separation or skipped-state parser exists in this branch.
claimAdjudication.alternativeExplanation: The skip notice is intentional operator feedback, and the packet may intend the JSON promise to apply only to validate.sh itself. That does not preserve the progressive wrapper's own JSON-mode stdout contract.
claimAdjudication.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade if the progressive CLI explicitly disclaims parseable JSON for skipped output or a consumer is shown to parse a separate JSON channel that carries the skip status.

findingDetails.title: Local audit consumers report an explicit skip as a pass
findingDetails.evidence: The skip producer returns exit 0 and emits `skipped: true, passed: true`. quality-audit.sh discards stderr, increments pass on exit 0, and writes JSON status `pass`; strict-pass-freshness.ts checks exit code and `passed === false` but ignores `skipped`, then returns status `pass`. The implementation summary says a skip is no evidence. The plan acknowledges these unchanged consumers, making this a disclosed but unresolved status mismatch. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/validate.sh:142-172] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/quality-audit.sh:125-150] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/sweep/strict-pass-freshness.ts:246-272] [SOURCE: specs/sk-doc/062-doc-validation-off-switches/implementation-summary.md:134-141] [SOURCE: specs/sk-doc/062-doc-validation-off-switches/plan.md:78-82]
findingDetails.recommendation: Surface skipped as a distinct status (or count) in local audit outputs so an opted-out run cannot be reused as validation evidence; keep the intentional local opt-out behavior documented.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The plan explicitly lists quality-audit.sh and strict-pass-freshness.ts as direct affected consumers and records their current pass behavior; the implementation summary separately states a skip cannot support a completion claim.

results.note: Claims are recorded but not independently rerun; checklist.md absent so AC_COVERAGE is exempt.

noveltyJustification: A direct producer-consumer trace exposed two distinct losses of explicit skip state outside the producer-level tests.
